item.title: Professor David Moher receives HKBU Honorary Doctorate and inaugural CEQC Award
item.dc:creator: UK EQUATOR Centre
item.description:
At the 67th Commencement of Hong Kong Baptist University (HKBU) on 16 November 2026, Professor David Moher received an Honorary Doctor of Science in recognition of his global leadership and capacity-building in scholarly guidance, results reporting, and transparent health research. Speaking on behalf of the honorary degree recipients, he highlighted how research transparency enables people to scrutinise and benefit from research findings. He also encouraged graduates to remain curious, think critically and use their knowledge with integrity in the service of the wider community.

Professor David Moher, Senior Scientist at the Ottawa Hospital Research Institute and Director of the Canadian EQUATOR Centre, has made leading contributions to the development and advancement of CONSORT (CONsolidated Standards of Reporting Trials) guidance and PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidance, helping to improve the completeness and transparency of health research reporting.

Inaugural CEQC International Award

The day before (15 November), Professor Moher received the inaugural CEQC International Award for Outstanding Contribution in Open Science and Evidence-Based Medicine. Established by the Chinese EQUATOR Centre (CEQC) at HKBU, the award recognises outstanding contributions to open science and evidence-based medicine. Following a nomination and voting process, the award committee selected Professor David Moher and Professor Youping Li (from Sichuan University, China), a pioneer in evidence-based medicine in China, as joint recipients.

The award was presented at the Evidence-Based Medicine and Reporting Guidelines International Conference and CONSORT Statement 30th Anniversary Celebration, held in Hong Kong on 15 November. Organised by CEQC, the conference brought together international scholars, clinicians, journal editors and policymakers under the theme “From Evidence to Impact: Strengthening Reproducibility and Transparency in Health Research”.

Following the award presentation, Professor Moher delivered a keynote lecture titled “The Evolution of Reporting Guidelines and the CONSORT Experience”. He also joined an interactive dialogue moderated by Professor Zhaoxiang Bian, Director of the CEQC. The discussion explored how clinical trial reporting has changed over the past 30 years, the responsibilities of interest-holders in promoting complete reporting, as well as the potential role of artificial intelligence in developing and overseeing reporting guidelines.

item.title: Welcome to the new EQUATOR Network website
item.dc:creator: UK EQUATOR Centre
item.description:
We are pleased to announce the launch of the redesigned EQUATOR Network website. The new site is designed to help researchers, authors, editors, peer reviewers and educators find the resources they need to improve the quality and transparency of health research reporting, faster than ever.

Since its founding, the EQUATOR Network has been a trusted source for reporting guidelines such as CONSORT, PRISMA and STROBE. As the library has grown, so has the need for a site that makes it simple to navigate. The new design puts users first, with clearer structure, improved search and a more modern look.

What’s new:

- Easier navigation: A faster way to search reporting guidelines and research reporting guidelines under development

- Refreshed toolkits authors, journals, peer reviewers and reporting guideline developers

- Improved look: a clean and modern feel to the website

Feedback

Tell us what you think via our contact page.

If you come across any deadlinks, also please let us know so we can fix them.
